# Retrospective: PR 12814

## What worked

Managed Herdr context and Team 4 ownership were verified before resetting either technical reviewer. Existing Claude Code authentication was retained for Opus, with new native sessions for both independent reviewers. Equivalent neutral inputs preserved independence. Targeted native QML state projection tested the intended lifecycle without exposing host desktop sockets. A no-behavioral-findings result remained acceptable, with one small documentation suggestion instead of speculative defects or generic test filler.

The coordinator read both full reports and material evidence, detected additional audit issues, and narrowed public claims rather than relying on a seal or parent exit alone. Fresh editorial passed the exact final draft. HTML is saved only; outer assistant owns presentation and publication.

## Deviations and remediation

- Astra performed named dependency-path discovery with host ls. It is conservatively recorded as an isolation-process deviation. All technical runtime evidence came from review.py. Corrected assignment now explicitly includes executable discovery, not only executable probes.
- Astra v1-v3 setup failures were retained, failed closed and excluded. Exact private root, qmltestrunner options and unique source extraction anchors should be established before assertions.
- Opus structural-01/02 failed fixture controls; later assertions in those cases do not count. History is preserved.
- Coordinator audit found Opus result writes without resolved private-root assertions, accumulating failed prerequisites, and nested qmllint pipe capture without direct retained streams. Parent runner logging is not nested-child streaming. This disproves its original blanket compliance claim; the audit addendum preserves the correction. Public technical evidence excludes those runs as runtime proof and excludes the lint claim.
- Actual lint output included import/type/override warnings, not only the categories summarized in the original final. This is corrected in synthesis, with no claim of real component validation.

See assignment-corrections.md for concrete instructions issued to the responsible reviewers. Failed evidence and original reports are not rewritten. The overall process is marked noncompliant despite a publishable scoped technical review.

## Why publication is not held for process alone

The valid Astra v4 fixture was separately inspected: private-root and final target assertions precede writes, prerequisites fail immediately, each child streams to retained files and has an explicit checked exit. Both revisions pass five actual lifecycle cases with negative and unchanged-path controls. Public claims are limited to that state projection and inspected source. Opus supplied an independent source review with the same no-behavioral-defect outcome and a source-backed documentation correction. No evidence of peer contamination or host mutation was found. No claimed compositor behavior rests on the invalid runs.

## Resources and carry-forward

No desktop, services, background daemons or shared test resources were allocated. Review runs complete in private namespaces. Reviewer panes and historical sessions are preserved, not restarted after this assignment. Source/evidence remains pinned. Cleanup uses owned receipts only, never host-wide process discovery. Use actual backend identities and limitations in all future evidence summaries. No Omadev bug was established and no infrastructure change was made.
comment:
No behavioral defect was established at `40c994b867e4` in the inspected source and targeted QML state checks.

**Verified:** the switch-close path now requests OnDemand keyboard focus and retains visibility until its 75 ms timer expires. Ordinary close still requests None immediately. Source-derived QML checks also covered reopening during retention and rapid reverse switching.

The following comparison describes requested state, not observed compositor focus:

| Outgoing panel | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Switching, with synthetic card opacity already zero | Focus None; no switch-close visibility hold | Focus OnDemand; visibility retained |
| Switch-close timer | 1 ms | 75 ms, then retention ends |
| Ordinary close | Focus None immediately | Unchanged |

**Documentation suggestion:** in [`KeyboardPanel.qml:91-93`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/40c994b867e46546340b0db3164fef5ce2ee7041/shell/Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml#L91-L93), describe a “75 ms grace period intended to cover the incoming panel's mapping” rather than “until the incoming panel takes it.” The timer does not observe whether the incoming panel has acquired focus.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source inspection and isolated, source-derived Qt/QML lifecycle checks on base and head. The checks used a stand-in QtQuick Item, synthetic focus modes and card opacity, not real Quickshell surfaces. Actual Hyprland focus continuity, Chromium flicker and desktop acceptance tests were not verified.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Opus 5 xhigh and Astra Xhigh technical reviews, followed by Astra synthesis against the saved source and targeted evidence.
